paper_title: Integrated Molecular, Interfacial, and Device Engineering towards High-Performance Non-Fullerene Based Organic Solar Cells
source_file: /home/wzfeng/MySearch/PhotoRag/MD/Advanced Materials - 2014 - Zang - Integrated Molecular  Interfacial  and Device Engineering towards High‐Performance/auto/Advanced Materials - 2014 - Zang - Integrated Molecular  Interfacial  and Device Engineering towards High‐Performance.md

knowledge_points.content: PBDTT-F-TT is a pseudo-two-dimensional (2D) conjugated polymer with alkylthienyl side chains, selected as a donor for its deep HOMO energy level and red-shifted absorption compared to PBDTTT-C-T.
knowledge_points.evidence: PBDTT-F-TT was selected because of its deeper HOMO and red-shifted absorption that form a better match with di-PBI compared to those for PBDTTT-C-T.

knowledge_points.content: The HOMO energy level of PBDTT-F-TT is -5.38 eV, which contributes to a higher open-circuit voltage (VOC) of 0.80 V in non-fullerene OSCs compared to 0.72 V for PBDTTT-C-T based devices.
knowledge_points.evidence: The HOMO energy level of PBDTT-F-TT was estimated to be around -5.38 eV... The devices with PBDTT-F-TT as donor have a significantly higher VOC (0.80 V) than the devices with PBDTTT-C-T (0.72 V), which is consistent with its deeper HOMO energy level.

knowledge_points.content: The optimized PBDTT-F-TT:di-PBI inverted organic solar cell with a SAM-modified ZnO interlayer achieved a maximum power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 5.90% and an average PCE of 5.73%.
knowledge_points.evidence: the average PCE of the SAM-modified device could be further increased from (5.28 ± 0.03)% to (5.73 ± 0.17)% [PCEmax of 5.90%].

knowledge_points.content: Optimal bulk-heterojunction (BHJ) morphology for the PBDTT-F-TT:di-PBI system was achieved using binary solvent additives consisting of 1.0% 1,8-diiodooctane (DIO) and 2.0% 1-chloronaphthalene (CN) in ortho-dichlorobenzene (oDCB).
knowledge_points.evidence: the photovoltaic properties can be significantly improved by using binary additives with 1.0% DIO and 2.0% CN in ortho-dichorobenzene (oDCB) (v/v).

knowledge_points.content: Inverted device architectures for PBDTT-F-TT:di-PBI show higher PCE (5.28%) than conventional structures (4.04%) due to superior light harvesting and more favorable exciton generation profiles centered in the BHJ layer.
knowledge_points.evidence: the average PCE of the inverted device ((5.28 ± 0.03)%) is much higher than that of the conventional one ((4.04 ± 0.07)%)... the inverted device shows higher exciton generation than the conventional device. Notably, the generated excitons in the inverted device are broadly distributed with a peak centered at the BHJ layer.

knowledge_points.content: The PBDTT-F-TT:di-PBI blend demonstrates highly imbalanced charge transport, with a hole mobility of 4.36 x 10^-2 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1 and an electron mobility of 3.32 x 10^-5 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1.
knowledge_points.evidence: The estimated electron mobility (μe)... is around 3.32 × 10^-5 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1, which is 3 orders of magnitude lower than that for hole mobility (μh = 4.36 × 10^-2 cm^2 V^-1 s^-1).

knowledge_points.content: PBDTT-F-TT:di-PBI devices processed from the non-halogenated solvent o-xylene achieved a PCE of 5.20%, demonstrating feasibility for environmentally friendly large-scale manufacturing.
knowledge_points.evidence: the performance of PBDTT-F-TT:di-PBI BHJ-based devices processed from o-xylene showed a quite high PCE of ca. 5.20%, which is comparable to that obtained using o-DCB.

knowledge_points.content: PC61BM-SAM modification on the ZnO interlayer suppresses interfacial trap-assisted Shockley-Read-Hall (SRH) recombination, as indicated by the reduction of the VOC light-intensity dependence slope from 1.46 kT/q to 1.10 kT/q.
knowledge_points.evidence: the device without SAM modification possesses a strong VOC dependence on light intensity with a slope of 1.46 kT/q... while the device with SAM modification shows a unique slope of 1.10 kT/q... the SAM-modified ZnO effectively passivates the inorganic surface trap states to suppress interfacial trap-assisted recombination.

knowledge_points.content: The PBDTT-F-TT:di-PBI system exhibits high thickness tolerance, maintaining an average PCE of 4.47% at an active layer thickness of 170 nm, which is approximately 80% of its peak efficiency.
knowledge_points.evidence: the PBDTT-F-TT:di-PBI device maintained ca. 80% of its PCE value as the BHJ thickness increased from 105 to 170 nm... an average PCE of (4.47 ± 0.07)% can be achieved in devices with a 170 nm thick BHJ layer.
